one_liner: Taste-first millet-based breakfast cereals and snacks for urban families, sold on its own site, Amazon and quick commerce.
sub_sector: Better-for-you packaged food (millet breakfast and snacks), D2C plus marketplaces
ask: INR 2.5 Cr at INR 14 Cr post-money
business_model: Sells seven millet SKUs (made by one co-packer) direct and via Amazon and quick commerce; 48% gross margin, 11% contribution after CAC and logistics.

founders.name: Ritu Hegde
founders.background_claimed: 6 years in category and brand roles at a large packaged-food company; food science training/degree.

founders.name: Sanjay Kulkarni
founders.background_claimed: 5 years in supply chain at a quick-commerce company; runs sourcing and the co-packer.

claims.text: 90-day repeat rate by cohort: 31% (June), 34% (July), 38% (August), from cohort data covering 3,100 customers.
claims.note: The deck shows only the best cohort (August, 38%); the form gives the full trend. The August cohort's 90-day window cannot be complete for customers acquired late in August if the data is as of October 2026, so 38% may be partial.

claims.text: Repeat trend is improving and above a founder-reported peer benchmark: Wild Date reports ~37% 90-day repeat, and the same page calls >30% within 90 days strong for a D2C food brand.
claims.note: Benchmark is anecdotal (one founder interview plus an unattributed FAQ line), not audited category data. GrainKind's 12-month target is 45% (D13).

claims.text: October 2026 revenue INR 16.5 L; INR 72 L cumulative since launch in November 2025; monthly revenue grew 4.8 -> 7.1 -> 10.2 -> 13.0 -> 16.5 (INR L) June to October.
claims.note: Consistent: June-October sums to INR 51.6 L, leaving INR 20.4 L for November-May.

claims.text: Gross margin 48% after COGS and packaging; blended CAC INR 340; contribution after CAC and logistics 11%; 12-month LTV:CAC about 1.8x.
claims.note: LTV:CAC 1.8x is thin for a brand and partly extrapolated (oldest cohorts are under 12 months old).

claims.text: First order does not pay back acquisition: average first order INR 540 at 48% gross margin is ~INR 259 gross profit against INR 340 blended CAC (INR 410 on paid social). June cohort averages 2.4 orders in 5 months.
claims.note: Derived from the founders' numbers. Payback depends on repeat holding.

claims.text: About 70% of new customers come through bought channels: paid social 45% (CAC INR 410) and quick commerce 25% (INR 290 after promos); nutritionist referrals 20% (INR 210), gyms and sampling 10% (INR 380).
claims.note: Echoes the Petalry precedent (C001: paid social ~2/3 of orders). Here, unlike Petalry, cohort repeat data is provided. Nutritionist referral is the cheapest channel but only 20%.

claims.text: Revenue mix: own site 55%, Amazon 25%, quick commerce 20%.
Seven products; three hero SKUs (Ragi choco crunch, Millet muesli, Jowar puffs) account for 87% of orders.
claims.note: Founders flag slower repeat on Jowar puffs, the quick-commerce favourite (F9).

claims.text: All products made by a single co-packer in Hosur; founders list single co-packer, rising paid-social costs and slower Jowar puffs repeat as key risks.
claims.note: Founders name their risks unprompted (R1-positive) and offer the co-packer agreement (F13).

claims.text: Priced at INR 62 per 100 g versus INR 45 for large cereal brands and INR 70 for other millet brands (founders' comparison).
Founder background differs slightly between documents: deck says Ritu Hegde is 'trained in food science'; form says 'Food science degree'.
claims.note: Minor wording difference rather than a contradiction; confirm the qualification.

claims.text: Founders: Ritu Hegde (CEO) claims 6 years in category/brand roles at a large packaged-food company; Sanjay Kulkarni (COO) claims 5 years in supply chain at a quick-commerce company. First-time founders, full-time since July 2025, team of 9.
Founder LinkedIn links are placeholders (*-example) and the website is a .example domain; no independent footprint for founders or brand found.
Founders surveyed 420 urban parents (July 2025) before launch.
Tata Consumer acquired 100% of Kottaram Agro Foods (Soulfull), a millet-based breakfast brand for kids and adults, in 2021.
claims.note: Direct category competitor (Soulfull Ragi Bites overlaps with Ragi choco crunch) backed by Tata distribution.

claims.text: Wholsum Foods (Slurrp Farm), a millet-led brand, reported FY25 revenue of Rs 97.5 crore (+33% YoY) and a net loss of Rs 32.67 crore.
claims.note: Benchmark: the scaled millet D2C peer is still loss-making at ~Rs 100 Cr revenue.

claims.text: ITC completed its acquisition of 100% of Yoga Bar (Sproutlife Foods) in September 2026.
claims.note: Large FMCG companies are consolidating the better-for-you snack/breakfast shelf - both competition and a possible exit route.

claims.text: The Indian healthy-snack shelf is described as increasingly crowded (Slurrp Farm, Early Foods, The Whole Truth, Farmley, Happilo named).
12-month targets: INR 40 L monthly revenue, 90-day repeat at 45%, contribution margin 15%; 40% of the raise goes to inventory and working capital.
Market sizing: INR 2,400 annual household spend is the founders' estimate from order data and a parent survey.
Sector as selected (Consumer brands) matches the business: a packaged millet food brand.
Raising INR 2.5 Cr at INR 14 Cr post-money; three food/retail angels have invested INR 45 L.
Founders offer to share the cohort sheet and the co-packer agreement.
